Both docstring inaccuracies are fixed (no code or tests changed):

### What changed
- **`src/mem_mcp/util_text.py` module docstring only.**
  1. Corrected the `slugs` table constraint from the inaccurate `^[a-z0-9-]+$` to the actual CHECK `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,62}[a-z0-9])?$`, and clarified that this constraint also caps length at 64 and rejects empty strings — neither of which `slugify_title` enforces, so callers storing into `slugs` must still handle empty results and the 64-char cap.
  2. Removed the false `SS → ß` example (because `"SS".lower() == "ss"`); kept `É → é`.

### Verification (exact output)

- `pytest tests/unit/test_util_text.py -q`
  ```
  19 passed in 0.09s
  ```
- `ruff check src tests`
  ```
  All checks passed!
  ```
- `ruff format --check src/mem_mcp/util_text.py`
  ```
  1 file already formatted
  ```
- `mypy`
  ```
  Success: no issues found in 333 source files
  ```

Nothing is left open — only the docstring was touched, and all new tests plus lint/format/types remain green.
